titre: Pfand -- la consigne, et une coutume de la ville
_histoire: Le gag : Mark jette sa bouteille vide dans une poubelle de rue ; un voisin
l'arrete -- << Das ist doch Pfand! >> -- vingt-cinq centimes la bouteille. Une
semaine plus tard il rapporte un sac a l'automate : une bouteille est refusee
(pas de consigne), le bon dit 2,40 EUR. Le soir, il pose la bouteille refusee
A COTE de la poubelle, pour ceux qui ramassent -- la coutume berlinoise. Le
voisin : << Jetzt sind Sie ein Berliner. >>
Ce qu'on apprend : das Pfand, die Flasche, die Dose, zurueckbringen, der
Pfandautomat, der Bon, der Muelleimer, der Spaeti, les prix (25 Cent, 2,40 EUR).
⚠️ LE VOISIN : PROPOSITION D'UN CAMEO. Le synopsis dit << un homme d'une
cinquantaine d'annees >>. Le cycliste de l'episode 3 (cycliste-jaune, voix
radfahrer-c) a cet age, habite le meme Kiez, et sa courbe est exactement
celle-ci : il arrete Mark sechement, puis il explique patiemment. Celui qui
a dit << Ganz Berlin hat Sie gesehen >> dit ici << Jetzt sind Sie ein
Berliner >> : la serie tient ses promesses de quartier (personnages.json,
_arc, point 3). Son velo appuye au mur et son blouson jaune le font
reconnaitre AVANT son visage. Si Jacques prefere un inconnu : voir
_si_nouveau_visage dans locuteurs.nachbar, rien d'autre ne change.
⚠️ PLAN 19, A TRANCHER : le rappel << Oder ein Pfannkuchen? >> suppose
l'episode 4. Pour qui ne l'a pas vu, c'est un mot drole sur un visage qui
rit -- l'humour de situation tient encore. Si Jacques le juge trop verbal,
l'episode se termine au plan 18, sans rien a reecrire.

nachbar._cameo: SI LE CAMEO EST RETENU : la voix du cycliste de l'episode 3 (Voice Design du 16 sept. 2026, apercu C, retenu par Jacques), telle quelle -- une voix qu'on a deja entendue est ce qui fait reconnaitre un personnage avant son visage. Le visage : personnages/nachbar.png, a DECOUPER (gratuit) dans video/episode-03-auf-dem-radweg/01-images/cycliste-serre.png -- acquis du 9 oct. : un secondaire devient recurrent en decoupant sa meilleure image. ⚠️ Sa chevelure n'a jamais ete vue (toujours sous le casque) : la feuille demande << short steel-grey hair >> comme la fiche de l'episode 3, et le casque pend au guidon du velo pour aider la reconnaissance.

portraits_a_faire.consigne: The man of the first reference picture, with exactly his face, his close-cropped grey beard and his thin rimless glasses, bareheaded with short steel-grey hair, sits on the wooden bench under the lit window of the shop shown in the second reference picture, in the evening. He wears the same bright yellow waterproof cycling jacket zipped to the collar, dark trousers. Seen from the hips up, a little left of centre in a vertical frame, the bottom edge of the picture crossing his thighs; the top of his head a hand's width under the top edge. One hand rests low in his lap, closed round the neck of a plain brown glass bottle with a small blank dark-green label; his other hand rests on the bench beside him. His face is turned three-quarters to the camera and his eyes look towards the RIGHT edge of the picture, sharp, eyebrows down, mouth closed. Left of him, against the wall, the handlebar of a dark city bicycle with a dark grey helmet hanging from it. Warm light from the window falls on him from the left. No readable text.

plans.de: Abend in Marks Kiez. Der Späti ist noch offen.
plans.fr: Le soir dans le quartier de Mark. Le Späti est encore ouvert.
plans.en: Evening in Mark's neighbourhood. The Späti is still open.
plans.consigne: Vertical 9:16 photo, as a passer-by would take it with a good phone camera from the opposite pavement of a narrow Berlin side street at dusk, looking straight at the front of a small corner shop (a Berlin Spaeti) -- the MASTER SET, empty of people. On the LEFT: a wide shop window lit warm yellow from inside, shelves of bottles and packets visible as plain colours, and under the window a weathered wooden bench against the wall. In the middle: the shop door, open, warm light spilling onto the pavement. On the RIGHT: the plain painted facade continues, a dark downpipe, and at the kerb a grey street-lamp post lit white with a plain ORANGE litter bin fixed to it at chest height, its round mouth open. Grey pavement slabs, cobbled kerb, deep blue sky above the roofline. The warm light comes from the LEFT; the shadows fall to the right. No readable text anywhere -- the window, the door and the bin carry no lettering.

plans.de: Ein Späti ist ein kleiner Laden. Er ist bis spät in die Nacht offen.
plans.fr: Un Späti, c'est une petite boutique. Elle est ouverte jusque tard dans la nuit.
plans.en: A Späti is a small shop. It stays open late into the night.
plans.consigne: Vertical 9:16 photo, a closer view of the lit window and open door of the same shop (reference: the master set), from the pavement in front: inside, shelves of bottles, cans, chocolate bars and crisps packets in plain bright colours, a cooler with bottles, a tired warm light; a cat asleep on the windowsill inside. The bench below the window is in the bottom of the picture, empty. No readable text: every label is a plain colour.

plans.de: Mark hat eine Limonade getrunken. Die Flasche ist leer.
plans.fr: Mark a bu une limonade. La bouteille est vide.
plans.en: Mark has drunk a lemonade. The bottle is empty.
plans.consigne: Vertical 9:16 photo (reference: personnages/Mark.png for the face, the master set for the place): the young man of the reference picture, in a plain dark burgundy crew-neck sweater and dark jeans, stands on the pavement at the street lamp on the RIGHT of the master set, right of centre, seen from the hips up, his face three-quarters to the camera, eyes towards the LEFT edge of the picture. His hand nearer the lamp holds an empty clear glass lemonade bottle with a small blank label just above the open round mouth of the orange litter bin, about to drop it in; his other hand hangs relaxed. Behind him the lit shop door and window. Evening, warm light from the left. No readable text.

plans.fr: Stop ! Mais c'est de la consigne !
plans.jeu: sec, indigne : la voix d'un voisin qui vous arrete parce qu'il faut bien que quelqu'un le fasse
fige, la bouteille au-dessus de la poubelle ; le mot est tout neuf pour lui

plans.de: Fünfundzwanzig Cent. Für die Flasche. Die bringen Sie zurück.
plans.fr: Vingt-cinq centimes. Pour la bouteille. Vous la rapportez.
plans.en: Twenty-five cents. For the bottle. You bring it back.
plans.jeu: la durete est deja partie : il explique, comme quelqu'un qui l'a fait mille fois

plans.de: Fünfundzwanzig Cent? Für eine leere Flasche?
plans.fr: Vingt-cinq centimes ? Pour une bouteille vide ?
plans.en: Twenty-five cents? For an empty bottle?

plans.de: Flaschen, Dosen – fast alle haben Pfand.
plans.fr: Les bouteilles, les canettes – presque toutes sont consignées.
plans.en: Bottles, cans – almost all of them carry a deposit.
plans.jeu: patient, presque content qu'on lui demande

plans.de: Mark behält die Flasche. Fünfundzwanzig Cent sind fünfundzwanzig Cent.
plans.fr: Mark garde la bouteille. Vingt-cinq centimes, c'est vingt-cinq centimes.
plans.en: Mark keeps the bottle. Twenty-five cents are twenty-five cents.
plans.consigne: Retouch of mark-muelleimer.png, ONE thing changes: the hand that held the bottle over the bin has drawn it back and holds it upright against his chest, and he looks down at it with a grin. The framing, the lamp, the orange bin, the shop behind him and his clothes stay exactly as they are. No readable text.

plans.de: Eine Woche später. Zwölf Flaschen, ein Beutel, ein Supermarkt.
plans.fr: Une semaine plus tard. Douze bouteilles, un sac, un supermarché.
plans.en: A week later. Twelve bottles, one bag, one supermarket.
plans.consigne: Vertical 9:16 photo, the entrance corner of a German supermarket under flat white ceiling light -- the SECOND MASTER SET, empty of people. On the LEFT, a bottle-return machine: a tall pale grey housing with a round dark opening at chest height, a small screen glowing a plain pale blue beside it, a round GREEN button under the screen and a narrow slot below. On the RIGHT, a pale wall and a stack of blue plastic crates; on the grey tiled floor in front of the machine, a plain navy blue cloth shopping bag full of empty bottles and cans, their necks standing out of the top. No readable text: the screen is a plain glow, the housing and the bag carry no lettering.

plans.de: Der Pfandautomat nimmt die Flaschen. Eine nach der anderen.
plans.fr: L'automate prend les bouteilles. L'une après l'autre.
plans.en: The deposit machine takes the bottles. One after the other.
plans.consigne: Vertical 9:16 close photo at the machine of the second master set: a man's hand with a dark burgundy sleeve pushes a plain brown glass bottle, bottom first, into the round dark opening; the bottle is half inside. The pale housing fills the background, the green button and the plain glowing screen visible at the left. No readable text.

plans.de: Eine Flasche kommt zurück. Kein Pfand.
plans.fr: Une bouteille revient. Pas de consigne.
plans.en: One bottle comes back. No deposit.
plans.consigne: Retouch of flasche-oeffnung.png, ONE thing changes: the bottle is now a clear glass lemonade bottle with a small blank label, and it has rolled back OUT of the opening into the open palm of the same hand, which catches it. The housing, the button, the screen and the light stay exactly as they are. No readable text.

plans.jeu: il parle a la machine, et il le sait

plans.de: Dann drückt er den grünen Knopf. Der Bon: zwei Euro vierzig.
plans.fr: Puis il appuie sur le bouton vert. Le bon : deux euros quarante.
plans.en: Then he presses the green button. The receipt: two euros forty.
plans.consigne: Vertical 9:16 close photo at the machine of the second master set: a man's index finger with a dark burgundy sleeve presses the round GREEN button; below it a small white paper slip is coming out of the narrow slot, blank. The plain glowing screen above. No readable text -- the amount is said by the narrator and shown in the subtitle, never printed in the image.

plans.fr: Deux euros quarante. Pour des déchets !
plans.jeu: ravi : le bon dit du vrai argent, et il y a une semaine tout ca etait des ordures

plans.de: Am Abend, wieder vor dem Späti. Der Nachbar sitzt auf seiner Bank.
plans.fr: Le soir, de nouveau devant le Späti. Le voisin est assis sur son banc.
plans.en: In the evening, outside the Späti again. The neighbour is sitting on his bench.
plans.consigne: Retouch of the master set spaeti-abend.png: the same framing, the same dusk, the same lit window and door, the same lamp and orange bin. Two people are added: on the bench under the window, the man of the second reference picture in his yellow jacket, his bicycle against the wall beside him; at the lamp on the right, the young man of the third reference picture in his dark burgundy sweater, the clear lemonade bottle in his hand, standing at the orange bin. They look at each other across the shop door. No readable text.

plans.de: Mark wirft die Flasche nicht weg. Er stellt sie neben den Mülleimer.
plans.fr: Mark ne jette pas la bouteille. Il la pose à côté de la poubelle.
plans.en: Mark doesn't throw the bottle away. He sets it down beside the bin.
plans.consigne: Vertical 9:16 photo, low, close to the pavement at the foot of the lamp post of the master set, at dusk: the clear lemonade bottle with its small blank label stands upright on the grey pavement slabs at the base of the grey post, and beside it, in the bottom right, the dark jeans and dark sneakers of the young man straightening up, his hand just letting go of the bottle neck. The orange bin on the post above, cut by the top edge. Warm light from the left. No readable text.

plans.de: Richtig so. Die holt jemand. Jetzt sind Sie ein Berliner.
plans.fr: C'est bien comme ça. Quelqu'un viendra la prendre. Maintenant, vous êtes un Berlinois.
plans.en: That's right. Someone will pick it up. Now you're a Berliner.
plans.jeu: il l'a adopte : approbation seche et chaleureuse a la fois ; la pointe reste pince-sans-rire
il rit : la semaine derniere, Berliner etait un beignet (rappel de l'episode 4 -- A TRANCHER, voir _histoire)
